newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen near highs above 114 after Japanese data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen near highs above 114 after Japanese data.

text.p: The dollar was in fine fettle and near peaks above 114 yen in early Europe, after a one-yen climb overnight, as gloomy output forecasts for Japan and rising unemployment dampened rate-hike expectations, said analysts.

"The industrial production numbers were strong, but the market chose to focus on the output forecasts for June and July, which were a fair bit weaker, and the jobless rate...They served to allay market fears of an imminent tightening in policy," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN AMRO.
A raft of Japanese data, including retail sales, industrial production and unemployment, were released in early Europe.

At 0845 GMT dollar/yen stood at 114.11/4.21 yen against 113.13/23 yen in late Europe on Thursday, though just off highs of 114.27 yen hit earlier in Europe. Dollar/mark was steady to a touch weaker, trading at 1.7258/63 against 1.7263/68.

Official data this morning showed May retail sales down by 1.8 percent, though key industrial output was up a preliminary 3.8 percent month/month in May. Japan's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 3.5 percent in May from 3.3 percent in April and matched the record high marked in May and June of last year. Pessimistic forecasts by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry for June and July output weighed on the yen.
While the dollar initially dropped overnight after the release of the industrial output figures, it quickly gained momentum as the market focused on the forward-looking data issued by the MITI.

The MITI's output forecasts showed a decrease of 2.6 percent in June and an increase of just 0.9 percent in July. Analysts also said comments by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita, the first since the release of the stronger-than-expected tankan survey late Wednesday, had also weighed on the yen.
Matsushita said if the official discount rate was raised prematurely it would negatively affect the economy.
But some, however, were surprised by the weakness in the yen against the dollar after such a strong tankan survey of business sentiment was released early on Wednesday.
The BoJ's diffusion index for big manufacturers, a key gauge of business confidence, rose to plus seven in June from plus two in March.

"I think we are getting all the time surprises on the strong side, rather than on the weak side. So maybe the market is under-estimating the underlying momentum of the economy. Although, one must admit that the picture for the moment is very patchy," said Ernesto Ramirez, economist at Bankers Trust.
Against the mark, however, the dollar was little moved in Europe, mostly ignoring France's admission late on Thursday it cannot meet the EMU deficit/GDP target.
Dollar/mark took its cue from a steady mark in Europe, little moved on its crosses, as it digested France's admission.

French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn, speaking on Thursday after European markets had finished trading for the day, said the nation's public deficit in 1997 would be more than three percent of GDP. He hastened to add that Paris was committed to joining the single EMU on time in 1999 and that the government had no intention of letting the deficit run out of control.
The market had long been expecting France to miss the three percent deficit-to-GDP target, considering it only a matter of time before this became public, analysts said.
Sterling pushed to new 59-month highs of 2.8660 marks in Europe after UK data.
